patches.reason: Chunks in the reserved vessel region must generate empty (no terrain, structures, features or mobs) with the void biome, so plots start clean and never get weather.

The sides of a vessel that lie on a chunk border of its plot are lit by the plot column next to them, which holds no block. When a chunk column's sky light is switched on, vanilla fills the all-zero light data already there for it with full sky light, down to the lowest section that is open to the sky; for a column without any block it computes that section from Integer.MIN_VALUE - 1, which overflows, and fills nothing. Such data is there when the vessel's own column came from the save first. The zeros stay on the server and are sent to every client: black sides until the vessel is loaded again. For plot columns the value is taken one higher, so every section is filled.
Players who were sent a vessel's plot chunks must receive block, block-entity and light updates of those chunks although they are far outside the player's view.
Every block change must reach Slipway so vessel collision shapes, mass, bounds and client meshes, and terrain bodies near vessels, are rebuilt.

The game decides whether an entity climbs from the block of the world its feet are in. A vessel's ladders, vines and scaffolding are not in the world where the vessel is, so they could not be climbed. When the world's block is not climbable, the feet are taken into each nearby vessel's plot and the block there is asked, with vanilla's own rules (the climbable tag, an open trapdoor above a ladder, nothing while gliding through a block that can be glided through).

patches.feature: deck riding, entity collision and dry hulls
patches.reason: Entities collide with vessel blocks in the vessel's frame, stand and walk on decks at any angle, slide off steep ones, and are carried by the moving vessel. An entity in air that a vessel's hull keeps the water out of (below the waterline of a floating hull, in the cabin of a submerged one) stands in water blocks of the world, which are still there: vanilla's look at the fluids around it is repeated with nothing to look at, so it does not swim, drown or get pushed by a current there.
All block reach checks (use, break, containers, menus, signs) must measure the distance to where a vessel block is in the world, not to its plot position.
Blocks placed on a rotated vessel are oriented by the player's facing in the vessel's frame.
Look-axis placement (logs, pistons, observers) on a rotated vessel follows the player's view in the vessel's frame.

patches.feature: drops, sounds, block events and effects on vessels
patches.reason: Entities spawned by vessel blocks (drops, experience, falling blocks) and sounds at vessel blocks must appear where the vessel is, not in its far-away plot. Block events (a chest's lid, a piston's stroke, a note) and level events (bone meal, dispenser smoke, block breaking) are what vanilla sends to the players within 64 blocks of the block, which for a plot position is nobody: they go to the vessel's viewers within 64 blocks of where the block is, with the plot position, where the client has the block.

Chests, barrels and ender chests look for the players who have them open in a box around the block every five ticks; for a vessel block that box is in the plot, so the lid shut a quarter of a second after opening. The box is put where the block is in the world.

Pistons are the one thing that moves blocks by itself; a move that would put the head or a block into the margin between plots, or so far out that the vessel would span more than the configured largest size (server side), is refused (as vanilla refuses to push past the build height), so a flying machine can never carry blocks into another vessel's plot or grow a vessel's bounds, tickets and mesh without limit.

A vessel's bounds must not grow past the configured largest size after assembly either (every column of the bounds is loaded, ticked, saved and sent to viewers). A block item placed by a player or a dispenser where its vessel may not grow to fails (decided on the server, at the position the item settles on, as vanilla fails above the build height), so the block and the item are not lost outside the vessel.

A player standing on a vessel has no world blocks around them; without this the server kicks them for flying after four seconds and logs and resends the air below them every ten seconds. The server also adds up a player's fall from the moves the client reports, in the world: on a vessel that is going down a jump counted as a fall of everything the vessel sank meanwhile, and the player landed hurt. For a player on a vessel the vertical part of each move is counted against the deck.

Vessel plot chunks are far outside the client's view-sized chunk storage; they are kept in a separate map so the client level has their blocks, block entities and light while terrain renderers never see them.
The crosshair must pick vessel blocks, in vessel space, so placing, breaking and using them works at any orientation.

patches.feature: sounds, particles and lighting on vessels
patches.reason: Sounds the client plays itself for its own actions at vessel blocks must play where the block is, and particles it makes there (a note, bone meal's sparkle) must appear there and not be dropped for being millions of blocks from the camera; when light data for a plot section arrives, the vessel mesh must be rebuilt (the terrain renderer that would be told never sees plot sections).

Particles made without the level's distance check (the chips of a block being mined or broken) and at a plot position are moved to where the block is, and every particle made for a vessel block gets its velocity turned with the vessel and the vessel's movement added.
Moving a particle from a plot to its vessel needs its position, its velocity and its previous position (or it would be drawn streaking in from the plot for one tick); the fields are protected.
Sounds the client plays directly at a block position (the thud of mining a block, a jukebox's music) bypass the level's sound method; at a plot position they are moved to where the block is.
A sound's position is set once in protected fields; moving it from a plot to its vessel needs to write them.

The view from inside a hull that keeps the water out must not be a view from under water (water fog, and whatever else asks the camera which fluid it is in, such as a shader pack's eye-in-water), although the world has water blocks there.

The game makes drifting specks (and the murmur of flowing water) in water blocks around the player. The world has water blocks in the air a hull keeps dry, so they would drift through a boat's hold and a submarine's cabin; there the game's ambient tick of the water is skipped.
Vessel blocks are outlined only when vanilla would outline a block (not with the HUD hidden, not where adventure mode forbids it, not when outlines are turned off), so they behave like world blocks.

hooks.access: reflection, guarded: when the methods are absent or fail, nothing waits for the terrain
hooks.reason: A disassembled vessel's picture is drawn until the terrain renderer has built the sections that got its blocks. With Sodium, vanilla's own question (LevelRenderer.hasRenderedAllSections) is never answered with yes, so Sodium is asked.

hooks.access: reflection, guarded: absent or changed fields are skipped
hooks.reason: Iris 1.11.6 never clears this map; its shader programs hold custom uniforms that capture the ClientLevel of the world they were built for, so every world opened with a shader pack stays in memory. It is cleared when no world is loaded (Iris rebuilds entries on demand). See DESIGN.md, world-retention RCA.
